Hi Liam — great to hear SupplyHub is moving quickly. Short answers up front: we can support both flows (self-billing marketplace routing or direct billing to end-sellers) but the required evidence and invoice layout differ. I've attached a short VAT onboarding checklist and our standard wire instructions for your AP team.

High-level options:
- Marketplace self-billing (recommended for multi-seller marketplaces): SupplyHub issues customer invoices; Redwood issues a single settlement invoice to SupplyHub. For reverse-charge to apply, we need SupplyHub's EU VAT registration + a signed marketplace attestation (template in the attached checklist).
- Direct billing to sellers: each seller must provide a valid EU VAT ID and we invoice each seller directly (adds friction but simpler tax reporting).

What we need from SupplyHub to enable reverse-charge on the settlement invoice:
1) Copy of SupplyHub VAT registration certificate (pdf)
2) Completed attestation form (I put a template in the checklist)
3) Confirmation of billing entity (SupplyHub legal entity name, VAT number, billing address)

Practical notes: we will include a clear reverse-charge note on our invoice ("VAT reversed under Article XX — recipient liable"). If SupplyHub prefers not to use reverse-charge, we can collect VAT at source but that will change settlement amounts and require collection of customer VAT rates by your platform.

Proposed next steps (mutual action plan):
- You upload VAT cert + sign attestation (SupplyHub) — target 3 business days
- Redwood tax ops reviews and confirms invoice template for reverse-charge — 2 business days
- First settlement cycle after confirmation: next monthly invoice run

If you want, I can loop in our tax lead (Ben) and our commercial lead (Grace) to finalize the routing and any minor contract language.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Sales \u2013 Redwood Inference

Marissa / Grace,

Forwarding Liam's question and your reply. Quick internal suggestion based on similar marketplace deals: 

- Opt for marketplace self-billing (one settlement invoice to SupplyHub). It reduces seller friction and centralizes collections for us.
- Require SupplyHub to provide the VAT cert + completed attestation before we flip to reverse-charge. Until we have cert, we bill with VAT collected at source (we'll need to collect company-level VAT rates from SupplyHub for accurate invoicing).
- Cashflow/credits: propose we keep net-30 for first two months to minimize AR risk, then move to standard net-45 after 2 successful settlements. We should reserve the right to suspend settlement if SupplyHub fails to provide VAT evidence within 14 days of onboarding.

Notes for contract redline: add a one-way indemnity for tax misreporting if SupplyHub fails to provide accurate seller VAT data. Also recommend we add an invoice comment field where SupplyHub can supply seller VAT IDs for reconciliation.

Happy to jump on a 30-min call with SupplyHub to walk through the checklist.

Ben
Head of Revenue Ops
ben_carter@redwood.ai
